Text.Text: Unmoving Center isn't a lesson anymore. It's just how you stand now. Keep it that way when the wind picks up.
You still need the wind to tell you where to stand. Come back when you don't.

You're still moving. Even standing still, you're moving. East of this farm, in the Anchorhead Canyon Range, the Canyon Drifters work the ground nearest the door wrong, mistaking fidgeting for stillness. Any Drifter counts, the whole range answers to one crew, but only one you put down with Sweeping Guard, Leg Sweep or Line Breaker, or while you stood inside your Shelter Circle. Put six of them down that way and bring me their Unmoving Center Canyon Range Tally, so I know it was you and not the wind.
Take the range key. Six Canyon Drifters, one tally, each put down with your guard and sweep or inside your Shelter Circle. Go.

The staff doesn't move. Everything moves around it. That's the whole trick: find the point that doesn't have to go anywhere, and let the fight orbit it. Most people spend years hunting motion. I'm done hunting.

The door is on the Anchorhead side of the Rocky Pass. Go out Anchorhead's Southern Entrance, through the town gate, and take the west trail into the pass; there's a sealed door a short walk south of where the trail comes in, against the pass's east bank. The canyons between here and there don't connect. That key opens it. Nothing else will.
Canyon Drifters, mostly. They still lean on their weight when they swing. You'll feel the wrongness in it before you see it.
Six Drifters. One tally. The range hasn't moved, and neither should you until it's done.
Six down, and the tally to prove it. Let's see it.
Recorded. The first stillness holds. Rest today; tomorrow the range gets harder to fool.

The Drifters were noise. Now go measure the ones who think they've already arrived. Five Canyon Sharpshooters deeper in the range mistake rigidity for stillness; they lock up and call it calm. They set their stances by an old sightline calibrator instead of feeling the line. Put five of them down, any Sharpshooter, by the same measures as the Drifters, and bring me the Unmoving Center Sightline Calibrator.
Five Sharpshooters, one calibrator. You know the door.
Rigidity isn't stillness. Rigid things shatter first. These Sharpshooters hold a pose and call it mastery. I've watched three of them crack under a first real hit. That's what you're going to test.
Same door, same key, same range. Go further in this time; the Sharpshooters don't set up near the entrance.
Better footwork than the Drifters, worse instincts. They've drilled the shapes long enough to look convincing at a glance.
Five Sharpshooters. One sightline calibrator. The range is exactly where you left it.
Five down, and their calibrator in your hand. Show me.
Recorded. You're not fidgeting either, not yet. Keep that.

Now the one who runs the floor. The warden, Range Warden Dorrim Vex, keeps the trial altar on the west side of the range, north of the door. Put him down and bring me his Unmoving Center Shattered Range Crest. Don't go alone. He has outlasted stronger arms than yours, each one standing by itself.
Bring two who can be still when you cannot. Alone, you're just one more thing for the warden to outlast.

He never flinches. Not before the hit, not after. That's not a boast. I've watched him take a blow that should have ended him and just keep standing. That's the discipline working, or something else wearing its face.
West side of the range, north of the door, by the trial altar. He's laid a ring of stones there and never steps out of it. He doesn't patrol. He waits for someone foolish enough to walk to him.

Bring company. Stillness holds when someone else is drawing the storm toward them instead of you. That's the only reason I send you with two others instead of alone. The warden won't wait for you to be ready.
The warden's still standing at his altar. Go back with company, and don't come back without his crest.
The warden's down and you're still standing. Let's see the crest.
Recorded. That's the first proof I didn't expect to see. Don't let it go to your head; the ones after him are worse.

Four High Table Guns run the inner ring now. His students, once. They drill the same stillness and call it a circle so no one has to stand alone in it. Go back to the range, put down all four, any High Table Gun, by the same measures, and bring me the Unmoving Center Marshal's Challenge Chit they've been trading between themselves like a trophy.
Four of them, one chit. Bring people who can watch your back while you watch theirs.
Students of a student. They learned the form secondhand and the fear firsthand. Four of them stand back to back and call that unity. It's just four people afraid to be still alone.
Same range, the deepest part of it. They've spread across it like it belongs to them because they showed up together. You'll find them.
Four means four angles at once. Bring your own circle, or you'll spend the whole fight turning.
The High Table Guns still hold the deepest part of the range. Four down, each by the same measures, one chit, then you're done there.
All four, and their chit besides. You've earned a look at it.
Recorded. There's one lesson left, and it isn't mine to give lightly. Rest first.

The master, Range Marshal Tarek Kor, is the reason I stopped teaching this to anyone who asked. He found the same stillness I did and never came back out of it. He hasn't taken a step in years, they say, and he doesn't need to. He waits in the Canyon Dueling Pit, through the door at the north end of the range. Go and end that. Don't go alone. Nobody has walked away from him by themselves, not once.
Bring your two. I'll be waiting for word either way.

A man who found the center and never left it. That's not victory, whatever it looks like from outside. I want you to stop him before stillness finishes swallowing him, or before he does the same to you.
The Canyon Dueling Pit, through the door at the north end of the range. The one place in that canyon that never moves, and neither does he.

Everything you're learning to do, he already does without trying. That's what I'm sending you to stand against, and why I'm telling you plainly: don't stand against it alone. Bring two you'd trust with your back. He's buried everyone who didn't.
He's still in the Dueling Pit, however he's standing. Go back when you have company.
He's not standing anymore. That's all the proof I need. Tell me it's done.
Recorded. The Unmoving Center is yours now, not mine, not his. Try not to let it swallow you the way it did him.
Anyway, the job.
Six Drifters. I can do that.
What's this stillness supposed to be, exactly?
Where do I find them?
What am I walking into?
Not yet.
Here's your tally.
Anyway, the job.
Five Sharpshooters, then.
What makes them different from the Drifters?
Same range?
What should I watch for this time?
I need a moment.
Here's the calibrator.
Back to it.
I'll bring people. Where's the warden?
What's different about the warden?
Where do I find him?
How many should I bring?
Give me time to find the right two.
His crest. We got him.
Back to it.
I'll gather my circle.
Who are they to you?
Where's their floor?
How many should I bring this time?
Let me find two I trust first.
Their chit. All four are down.
Back to it.
I'll bring two. Tell me where he is.
What am I actually ending?
Where does he wait?
What is he going to do?
I need to find two people who'd walk in there with me.
It's done. He's not standing.
